concepts.def: Family vocab: los padres (parents), los hermanos (siblings), los abuelos (grandparents), los primos (cousins).
Relationships: 'Me llevo bien con...' (I get on well with...), 'Discuto con...' (I argue with...).
Reflexive verbs use pronouns me/te/se/nos/os/se: llevarse bien, pelearse (fight), casarse (get married).
Two verbs for 'to be': ser (permanent: 'Soy alta'), estar (temporary/location: 'Estoy cansado').
Adjectives agree in gender and number: simpático/simpática/simpáticos/simpáticas, joven/jóvenes.
tú = informal singular (friends/family), usted = formal (strangers/teachers). 'Usted' uses 3rd person verb.

walkthroughs.body_html:
Theme 2: Lifestyle and Wellbeing — a core area of GCSE Spanish.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Theme 2: Lifestyle and Wellbeing brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with Theme 2: Lifestyle and Wellbeing.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.

mcqs.q: Which sentence correctly says 'I get on well with my sister'?
options: Me llevo bien con mi hermana.
Me llevo bueno con mi hermana.
Yo llevo bien con mi hermana.
Me llevar bien con mi hermana.

mcqs.q: Which is the correct use of ser/estar: 'I am tired'?
options: Estoy cansado.
Soy cansado.
Estás cansado.
Eres cansado.

mcqs.q: How do you say 'I am going to visit Spain' in Spanish?
options: Voy a visito España.
Voy visitar España.
Voy a visitar España.
Accents are random in Spanish.

mcqs.q: How do you say 'I don't see anything' in Spanish?
options: Veo nada.
No veo nada (double negative is correct).
No veo algo.
Voy a visito España.

mcqs.q: Why does 'qué' have an accent in '¿Qué quieres?' but not always elsewhere?
options: Accents are random in Spanish.
It is a mistake.
The accent distinguishes interrogative/exclamative 'qué' from relative 'que'.
Voy a visito España.
